verdict: Avoid new unsecured handicraft/carpet exposure in Srinagar; lend only to GI-certified, toolkit-supported units with tight stock-and-receivable control.
title: Srinagar Handicrafts & Carpets: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Srinagar carpet or Pashmina unit buys raw wool or yarn, pays master artisans by the piece, and sells finished pieces to exporters and showrooms months later.** Cash leaves at the loom and returns at the shipping bill, so the working-capital cycle is long and the inventory is the collateral. **The value sits in the finished, authenticated piece, not the loom** — which is why GI testing volumes matter to us. [1]

## What has changed now
**The local demand signal is negative: J&K GST collections are -10.6% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and electricity demand is -0.5% against India +9.5% [D].** That is a state-level stress read, not a Srinagar-specific one — the sources say little about this city, so lean on first principles and peers. **Peer results confirm the squeeze: Golden Carpets' Q1FY27 revenue fell 53.6% YoY to ₹12.05 lakh with a ₹7.31 lakh net loss [5], and Priti International's revenue contracted 66.59% YoY with operating margin at -3.78% [4].** Both are dated 2026 and are the clearest read we have. **Nationally, bank credit is +26.8% YoY against output +3.8% [D] and repo is 5.5% on a tightening stance [D]** — so any handicraft proposal priced off old assumptions is underpriced.

## Where the growth is
**The one live positive is authentication: GI testing is projected to nearly double to 42,000 in 2026-27 from 22,351 in 2025-26, with the daily rate up to around 170 from 75-85 [1].** Separately, the Textiles Ministry has released ₹30.46 lakh under NHDP for toolkits and skill training across carpet, Sozni, Papier Mache and walnut carving [2][3]. **So pursue the GI-certified Pashmina, Kani and Sozni units and the toolkit-supported artisan clusters; avoid the plain reseller and the unauthenticated grey-market trader.** When a proposal lands, check the GI test certificate and QR coding before sanctioning; if the borrower cannot show certification, ask why and price for the risk.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the inventory, not the balance sheet: hypothecation of stock, receivables-backed drawing power, and no clean unsecured limits.** Rating methodology is explicit that inventory management while sustaining scale is the key sensitivity [9] and that high leverage leaves a unit vulnerable in a downturn [8][10]. **Take stock statements and GI test counts every month, and receivables ageing every quarter.** If the drawing power falls below the limit, ask for the shortfall in cash before renewing.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the monthly GI test count at the unit, the stock-turn days, and the export receivable ageing.** If test volumes stall while stock rises, the unit is holding unsold inventory — stop fresh disbursement and inspect the godown. If a borrower's revenue falls at the pace of the peers above [4][5], move to secured-only. **The data call is Avoid at 29 [D]; the local news is mixed but the state demand signals are worse, so the call stays Avoid for unsecured and selective for certified units.**
